walkthroughs.body_html:
Atomic & Nuclear Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atomic & Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atomic & Nuclear Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which subatomic particle has negligible mass?
options: Proton
Neutron
Electron
Nucleus

mcqs.q: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed atoms are:
options: uniformly dense spheres
mostly empty space with a tiny positive nucleus
made entirely of electrons
made of plums in pudding

mcqs.q: In a balanced nuclear equation, what must be equal on both sides?
options: Only the atomic number (proton count) needs to balance.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
The total mass number (top numbers) and the total atomic number (bottom numbers) must both balance.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between nuclear fission and fusion?
options: Fission and fusion are the same process, just at different scales.
Fission splits a heavy nucleus into smaller ones; fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.
It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Nucleus”?
options: Tiny dense central region of an atom (~10⁻¹⁵ m) containing protons and neutrons.
Rutherford's gold-foil scattering replaced the plum pudding model with a small, dense, positive nucleus.
Negatively charged particle orbiting the nucleus in shells; relative mass ~1/2000.
Smallest unit of matter that keeps the properties of an element; ~10⁻¹⁰ m across.

Positively charged particle in the nucleus; relative mass 1, relative charge +1.
Smallest unit of matter that keeps the properties of an element; ~10⁻¹⁰ m across.

mcqs.q: An atom of chlorine has 17 protons and a mass number of 35. How many neutrons does it have?
options: 17 neutrons
13 neutrons
21 neutrons
18 neutrons
